--- title: "Water Quality Data" --- CMAR collects high-resolution (10 minutes to 1 hour) temperature, dissolved oxygen, salinity, and sensor depth data through the Coastal Monitoring Program. # Data Collection Water Quality data is collected using moorings referred to as “sensor strings”. A typical sensor string configuration consists of a rope attached to the seafloor by an anchor and suspended by a sub-surface buoy, with sensors attached at various depths (@fig-sensor-string). Most strings deployed since 2018 are attached to the anchor by an acoustic receiver with a release mechanism, which allows the mooring to be retrieved without a diver or winch. The receiver also logs detections of tagged animals including great white sharks, sturgeon, and tuna for the [Ocean Tracking Network](https://oceantrackingnetwork.org/). ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![Diagram of a typical sensor string configuration (not to scale).](figures/sensor_string2.png){#fig-sensor-string fig-align='center' width=487} ::: ::: Characteristics of the station location (e.g., depth, bottom type, and currents) and stakeholder needs dictate the string design (e.g., anchor weight, and number/type of sensors). Sensor strings are generally deployed 200 m to 1000 m from shore, in depths up to 75 m. Historically, strings were deployed with only temperature sensors, but in more recent years at least one dissolved oxygen sensor is included (typically at 5 m). At the request of industry, salinity sensors are also included at stations near proposed and existing shellfish aquaculture leases. Some of the sensors used to measure these variables also measure sensor depth, and CMAR has also processed and published this opportunistic depth data. The sensor string configurations are described in @tbl-configs and shown in @fig-sensor-string-configs. For configurations that float with the tide, sensors remain at a roughly constant depth below the surface. For fixed configurations, the sensor depth below the surface changes with the tide. | Configuration | Description | Floats with tide? | |:---|:------------|---| | Sub-surface buoy | Attached to a sub-surface buoy. Typically has an acoustic release, but is sometimes retrieved by a diver or drag line. | No | | Attached to fixed structure | Attached to a wharf, bridge, or pole. | No | | Surface buoy | Attached to a surface buoy. | Yes | | Attached to gear | Typically attached to aquaculture gear, but may be attached to another floating structure. | Yes | | Floating dock | Attached to a floating dock. | Yes | | Unknown | Configuration not indicated in the deployment log. | Unknown | : Sensor string configurations. {#tbl-configs}
::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![Diagram of different sensor string configurations (not to scale).](figures/sensor_string_configurations.png){#fig-sensor-string-configs fig-align='center' width=1152} ::: ::: # Sensor Validation Prior to deployment, the sensor calibration is validated using a simple cooler test. Code to run the validation test is published in CMAR’s R package [`calval`](https://github.com/centre-for-marine-applied-research/calval). The [CMAR Sensor Validation App](https://cmar-calval.share.connect.posit.cloud/) provides a user interface for running the code. ## Pre-Deployment Validation Sensors are set to record at 10 - 15 minute intervals and submerged in a well insulated container (cooler) of water for at least 24 hours. Seawater is used for tests with salinity sensors. After the recording period, data from all sensors is offloaded. Each observation is compared to the median value of all sensors in the container. Sensors with > 10% of measurements outside of the acceptable range indicated in the sensor manual are re-validated. A temperature or salinity sensor that fails 2 consecutive validation tests is sent to the manufacturer for maintenance. Dissolved oxygen sensors are included in the validation test, but do not reliably pass. Sensors in the same cooler at the same time show different magnitudes and trends in dissolved oxygen. It is not feasible to re-test all sensors that fail, and so they are deployed regardless of the validation results. The observations undergo strict quality control on retrieval. ![Four aquaMeasure DOT sensors, 3 hobo sensors, and 1 VR2AR sensor submerged in water in a cooler for a validation test.](figures/val_cooler2.jpg){#fig-cooler width=60% height=60%} ## Post-Deployment Validation Retrieved sensors undergo a post-deployment validation test, which follows the same procedures as the pre-deployment validation test. The post-deployment tests identify sensors that drifted, were impacted by biofouling, or were damaged. # Data Access Coastal Monitoring Program Water Quality Data can be accessed from several platforms. Summary reports are available on the [CMAR Data Access Map](https://cmar.ca/coastal-monitoring-program/). Full data sets can be downloaded from the [Nova Scotia Open Data Portal](https://data.novascotia.ca/browse?tags=coastal+monitoring+program) and the [CIOOS Atlantic](https://catalogue.cioosatlantic.ca/organization/cmar). ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](figures/data_access.png){fig-align='center' width=2200} ::: :::
